asserts: A re-run whose environment holds a variable rule v1 redacted, and whose digest could not be compared -- the two recordings were keyed by two different stores -- is GRANTED its licence and told exactly what was not checked. A check that could not run is not a finding against the pair (the rule `refocus_licence` already applies to a recorder that declares it captures no output), so the marker rides `refocus_licence_unverifiable` and `info` replays it in short form, `licence unverifiable: env (redacted, not comparable)`, while the NAMES ride the verified fact -- `1 redacted variable(s) not comparable (different keys): SECRET_TOKEN` -- because a variable the tool stopped checking is one a reader is owed the name of. The marker is fixed text carrying no names on purpose: `relicense` filters caveats by exact string, and a marker carrying names would never match itself. A digest that DIFFERS is a different outcome and withholds exactly as a changed variable does; this vector pins the third case, which is the one that must not be mistaken for either of the other two.

refocus_licence_verified: identical call shape across 1 compared fingerprint(s), holding 2 causal event(s)

2 environment variable(s) compared and unchanged in the environment the rerun executed under; not compared: OLDPWD, PWD, SENSORIUM_DIR, SHLVL, _; 1 redacted variable(s) not comparable (different keys): SECRET_TOKEN
refocus_licence_unverifiable: env: unverifiable in part (redacted variables not comparable)

questions.ask: A re-run holds a redacted variable whose digest cannot be compared: does the licence still stand, is the reader told which check did not run, and is the variable named?
expect_contains: 1 redacted variable(s) not comparable (different keys): SECRET_TOKEN
